component.name: Manic Microbes
component.summary: Watch evolution happen in a closed jar

description.p: An artificial life simulator in the lineage of Tierra, Avida and DarwinBots, and a piece of consumer software about looking at one. Cells carry a genome of byte-encoded instructions and execute it in a virtual machine of their own. The genome builds and controls physical machinery — organelles — rather than expressing behaviour directly.

They live on a substrate carrying a fluid with sixteen diffusing chemicals and an incident light field. Matter is exactly conserved. Energy arrives as light and leaves as heat. Cells eat, move, sense, attack, join, differentiate and divide.

There is no fitness function anywhere in it and there never will be. Nothing is scored. Selection is a consequence of the physics, and that constraint is enforced by tests rather than by good intentions.
Two ways to use it, sharing one engine:

ul.li: Set up a world, walk away, and read the wiki it writes about its own species
Write cells by hand in an assembly language, and watch whose code survives

screenshot.caption: Four hundred cells and sixty distinct genomes, a thousand ticks after one ancestor

description.p: The first release with anything to download. Pre-release still: no stable save format, so a slide written by one version may not open in the next.
